back: Verbs like 'give' can have two passive forms (e.g., 'We were given that vase' or 'That vase was given to us') [2].
Verbs like 'explain' or 'suggest' only have one passive form: 'The problem was explained to me' [2].
Verbs like 'elect' or 'appoint' have one passive form (e.g., 'She was elected president') [2].
Active verbs followed by object + bare infinitive (feel, hear, help, make, see) take a to-infinitive in the passive [2].
Transitive two- and three-word verbs can often be made passive (e.g., 'He was looked after') [2].
Verbs like 'come up against' or 'brush up on' are NOT used in the passive [2].
Some phrasal verbs like 'put out' (extinguish) can be passive, but not 'put out' (reach out a hand) [2].
I was handed a note / A note was handed to me [3].

front: They made him return the money.
back: He was made to return the money [2].
phased out -> The product was phased out [3].
